subject: Urgent: p99 latency spikes & error surge after model swap — Aurelia Therapeutics
messages:
From: Sara Lincoln <sara.lincoln@aurelia.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-06T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API errors & latency spike after today's model swap

Evelyn —

We started seeing a heavy increase in p95/p99 latency and intermittent 502/504 errors right after the model swap that happened at ~07:00 UTC this morning. Traffic volume is comparable to baseline, but tail latency blew up (p99 ~ 1.8s -> 4.6s) and throughput dropped as many client requests timed out. We've attached a small sample of timings from our side.

This is impacting two production features (clinical note generation + anonymization); customers are getting timeouts. Please escalate — Aurelia is asking for an interim mitigation and a post-incident plan.

Attachments: aurelia_latency_dump_0306.csv

— Sara
Sr. Platform Engineer, Aurelia Therapeutics
ops@aurelia.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-06T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: API errors & latency spike after today's model swap

Team — FYI, Aurelia reported a p99 jump and 502s immediately after we rolled v3.4 as the default backend for hosted-api (canary finished at 06:55 UTC). Attached their timing sample.

Quick asks:
- Marcus/Jasmine: can you confirm whether the v3.4 kernel selection or new quantization path caused any CPU fallback / slow path on the serving hosts? Look at the 06:40–08:00 window for p95/p99 and KV cache hit rates.
- Ben/Sean: this is customer-facing; Aurelia is already calling their CTO. Please prep an interim customer statement and expectations on credits if we need a rollback.

I will patch the routing policy to split traffic back to v3.3 if we confirm regression, but want root-cause before full rollback.

—Evelyn
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: API errors & latency spike after today's model swap

Evelyn / Jasmine —

Preliminary triage: host traces show elevated CPU stalls on a subset of our older A100 pool where the new quantization kernel path for v3.4 triggers a less-optimized matmul fallback (rare code path). That fallback increases single-request latency variance and causes the KV cache prefetcher to fall behind under bursty traffic — leading to more requests hitting the slower attention path.

I attached a flamegraph from 06:50–07:05 showing the time spent in the fallback path (flamegraph_0307.png). We can mitigate with two short-term actions:
1) Push a routing policy patch to reduce v3.4 weight to 0% for the affected HW class (will take ~7 minutes to propagate).
2) Apply a targeted kernel override to force the older optimized matmul path for v3.4 on A100 hosts until we ship a proper fix (hotpatch; ~45–60 min rollout).

I recommend implementing (1) immediately and (2) as a follow-up.

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia — customer escalation & exec ask

Evelyn / Sean —

Aurelia's CS team pinged their execs within 30 minutes; they're requesting a formal statement and are asking about credits for downtime. If we move fast with a rollback or traffic split, they may accept a mitigation + credit instead of a full rollback.

Can we commit to:
- Immediate routing split away from v3.4 for affected host class (Marcus)
- Customer-facing note in the next 30 minutes acknowledging impact + expected time to mitigation (Evelyn / Sean)
- Headline for execs with mitigation + next steps and a timeline for postmortem (I can draft)

Ben
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lincoln <sara.lincoln@aurelia.ai>, ops@aurelia.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-06T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API errors & latency spike after today's model swap — immediate mitigation

Sara — thank you for the sample and for flagging this. We're escalating with highest priority. Short update and actions we've taken: 

1) We've pushed a routing policy to reduce v3.4 traffic to 0% on the affected GPU class; we expect the change to finish propagating within ~10 minutes. This should restore baseline p95/p99.
2) Marcus's team is preparing a hotpatch to force the older optimized matmul path; target deploy in ~45–60 minutes.
3) We'll run a controlled canary of the hotpatch on a small pool before wider rollout.

We will follow with a postmortem and timeline for remediation. I appreciate your patience — I'm on the call with Marcus's team now.

Attachment: routing_policy_patch.diff

—Evelyn
VP, Customer Reliability
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lincoln <sara.lincoln@aurelia.ai>, ops@aurelia.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-08T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update & next steps — Aurelia customer impact (SUP-98214)

Sara / Aurelia team —

Follow-up after our mitigation and investigation:

Summary:
- Root cause: an untested execution fallback in the new v3.4 kernel path that triggers on our older A100 host variant, increasing tail-latency under bursty traffic.
- Immediate mitigation applied 2028-03-06 10:18 UTC: routing policy removed v3.4 from affected host class; this restored p95/p99 to baseline within ~12 minutes.
- Hotpatch deployed 2028-03-06 11:12 UTC to the small canary pool and then rolled to remaining hosts; full fix shipped to serving fleet by 2028-03-06 12:05 UTC.

Customer remediation & next steps:
- We've opened SUP-98214 and will provide a detailed postmortem by 2028-03-12.
- Redwood will apply a service credit for the impacted window; Ben will follow up on the commercial details.
- We will add an automated compatibility check for kernel fallback patterns to our model onboarding flow to prevent similar regressions.

Attachments: flamegraph_0307.png (triage artifact)

Apologies again for the disruption — we take these incidents seriously. We will share the postmortem and the remediation timeline within the week.

—Evelyn
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
